outputs.summary: Added resolveLaunchFolder(chat, deps) in src/main/agents/launchFolder.ts. It takes the real path of the chat's folder and requires that it exists, is a directory, equals the canonical path the chat stored (so a symlink swapped in is refused) and is still tracked (deps.trackedFolder, wired to FolderRegistry.resolve in bootstrap). Otherwise it throws DomainError('not_found', 'The folder <path> <reason>. Track the folder again to keep using this chat.'). The session manager has a new required dependency, folders: LaunchFolderDeps. startedSession, the single path for the first message, a new process after an idle stop or model change, retry, start-on-open and Start run's orchestrator chat, runs the check before issuing the grant. It passes the result as folder to issueChatCli and startOptions, so the spawn cwd, the protocol's workspace and dm --repo are one string. A refused start issues no grant and creates no adapter. The adapters restart processes themselves (after a crash, and for Cursor after a model change) without going back through the session manager, so ChatAdapterStartOptions gained checkFolder(): () => void. The Claude (launch), Codex (open) and Cursor (connect) adapters call it before every process they start; a failure rejects that turn, and the session manager stores it as the chat's usual error item. A refusal at the first message rejects send with the DomainError and stores nothing, matching other failed starts. That lets Start run remove the orchestrator chat and report the reason, and lets the renderer show the error while keeping the composer text. docs/architecture.md has a new 'The chat's folder' paragraph.

discoveries.body: Quitting with a live agent process logs 'Uncaught exception: Error: database is not open' from SqliteDb.close. bootstrap.ts runLifecycle closes appDb on every before-quit; quitDisposal's disposeBeforeQuit cancels the first before-quit (busy), disposes the chats and calls app.quit() again, so appDb.close() runs twice. The first before-quit also closes workspaces and app.sqlite before agent disposal finishes. Seen in DM-248 runs 1 and 3 (DM-248-app-run1.log, -run3.log); log line only, exit code 0.
discoveries.title: Close app.sqlite once on quit when chats are live

discoveries.body: resolveLaunchFolder runs only when a process starts. In DM-248, after scratch-a was renamed, the chat whose claude process was live kept answering, and lsof showed its cwd in scratch-a-renamed (DM-248-ps-c4-live-process-after-rename.txt). The pin holds only until the next start, so an agent can keep working in a folder that is no longer the tracked one.
discoveries.title: Stop or refuse a live chat agent whose folder was moved

discoveries.body: chatStore.ts locate() keys chats by canonicalPath(ref.folder). After the folder is replaced by a symlink to another directory, the chat handlers fail with 'Chat not found: <id>' before the session manager runs, so the person never sees resolveLaunchFolder's message naming the folder and the reason. The start is still refused.
discoveries.title: Name the folder when a chat's folder was replaced by a symlink

discoveries.body: chatHandlers.ts trackedFolder() refuses any chat request for an untracked folder with the generic 'That folder is not tracked by Dark Mechanicus.' before the session manager runs, so resolveLaunchFolder's '… is no longer tracked. Track the folder again…' message never reaches the app.
discoveries.title: Name the folder when a chat request is refused for an untracked folder

discoveries.body: cliInstructions (the exact dm command line, including --repo) is appended only to Claude's system prompt (claude.ts systemPrompt.append). codex.ts and cursor.ts never send options.instructions, so those agents get DM_SESSION_TOKEN in their environment but are never told the command; cliInstructions.ts says an agent without it concludes it has no access. The Autonomous ACP adapter will hit the same gap.
discoveries.title: Tell Codex and Cursor chats the dm command they may run

discoveries.body: At quit with scratch-a renamed, disposeSession's revokeChatGrant failed with 'DomainError: … scratch-a is not initialized for Dark Mechanicus' (DM-248-app-run1.log), and the worker grant stayed unrevoked in scratch-a's state.sqlite until it expired 12 h later. Pre-existing code.
discoveries.title: Revoke a chat's grant even when its folder is gone at dispose

discoveries.body: After DM-251, renderer agentName(id) returns 'Custom agent' for cu_ ids in ChatHeader, chatMeta, runBarView, ChatRow, SignedOutCard and workspaceActions, which have only the chat record. Once custom CLIs exist (DM-260/261), these should take the connected AgentView or a display-name lookup.
discoveries.title: Show a custom agent's display name where only the chat record is at hand

discoveries.body: In DM-253's recording, with --approval-mode always-ask, a8s answered the hello.txt write with tool_call_update failed 'Tool call denied by user: write' and no session/request_permission, after asking for pwd. The cause is unverified (the always-ask policy for writes in ACP mode, or the client's fs.writeTextFile:false). DM-259 must know before it relies on file edits; see docs/reports/autonomous-acp.md.
discoveries.title: Find out why a8s refuses a file write under always-ask without asking

discoveries.body: killProcessTree returns false when the process group is still alive after its one-second wait, but nodeTransport.kill ignores that result, so its comment that the kill resolves once the tree is gone is not true under load. Seen as DM-254 Fireguard run 2's flake (acpProcess tree-kill test, run 28 of 100).
discoveries.title: Report when an agent's process tree outlives kill

discoveries.body: electron-log writes to ~/Library/Logs/dark-mechanicus/main.log whatever --user-data-dir is, so DM-248's isolated test instances appended to the person's own app log. End-to-end runs cannot fully isolate from the person's profile.

content.summary: Sprint 1 delivered the local half of Agent CLIs. Connected agents now live in a new app-wide SQLite database (app.sqlite in user data, with its own migrations), and a profile's agents.json is imported once and deleted. Every agent has an id and a protocol: adapters, chats, sign-in flags and IPC address agents by id, and a chat's adapter is chosen by its agent's protocol. Every chat process is pinned to its canonical folder, which is checked on every start, and Autonomous's ACP surface is recorded for the sprint 2 adapter. All six work tickets and the acceptance node were accepted on their first attempt. Fireguard graded A (92) on its third run, the Definition of Done passed, and the sprint landed as 027f042 on agent-clis. Gaps found and carried into sprint 2 as discoveries: a double app.sqlite close when quitting with a live chat (log line only), a live agent that keeps running in a moved folder until its next start, and generic error text for symlink-swapped or untracked folders.
